world.setting: Cincinnati, Ohio, after the Civil War; 124 Bluestone Road; Sweet Home, Kentucky as the remembered plantation
world.register: literary, documentary, slow and heavy; a critical analysis of a novel, not a ghost story trailer

sethe.name: Sethe
sethe.role: the mother at 124 Bluestone Road, who killed her baby daughter rather than see her returned to slavery
sethe.look: a Black woman in her late twenties, slim and strong, dark brown skin, hair tied back in a cloth, a faded plain cotton dress, a long pale scar of a chokecherry tree across her upper back

denver.name: Denver
denver.role: Sethe's daughter, raised in isolation at 124 Bluestone Road, the one who walks out to the steps for help
denver.look: a young Black woman around twenty, thin, dark brown skin, hair in braids, a simple grey dress with a shawl

paul-d.name: Paul D
paul-d.role: a man who was enslaved at Sweet Home with Sethe, who returns to 124 Bluestone Road in 1873
paul-d.look: a Black man in his late thirties, broad shouldered, dark brown skin, short hair, a worn brown work coat over a plain shirt

baby-suggs.name: Baby Suggs
baby-suggs.role: Sethe's mother-in-law, an old preacher who gathers people in the Clearing
baby-suggs.look: a Black woman in her sixties, small and stooped, grey hair under a white headscarf, a long dark dress and apron

beloved.name: Beloved
beloved.role: a young woman who appears at the house, who may be the returned daughter or a ghost
beloved.look: a young Black woman in her early twenties, pale dark skin, long hair loose, a plain white dress, barefoot

schoolteacher.name: The schoolteacher
schoolteacher.role: the white man who runs Sweet Home, who records the enslaved people in a ledger of their traits
schoolteacher.look: a white man in his fifties, neat dark suit, starched collar, a black tie, clean-shaven, a notebook in his hand

stamp-paid.name: Stamp Paid
stamp-paid.role: a man who ferried escaping enslaved people across the river and later shows Paul D a newspaper clipping
stamp-paid.look: a Black man in his fifties, lean, dark brown skin, a grey waistcoat and an old hat

kitchen.look: 124 Bluestone Road: a plain wooden kitchen with a table and a stove, the house that holds the family's history

forest.look: the Clearing in the woods where Baby Suggs preaches, dappled light under the trees

shore.look: the Ohio river bank where the escape crossing happens

room.look: the schoolteacher's study at Sweet Home, lined with a ledger and papers

street.look: a dirt road leading up to 124 Bluestone Road in Ohio

spine.claim: The book is a ledger: slavery counted people as property, and the novel asks what a mother counted as love.
Sethe's choice of a grave over a bill of sale is the impossible arithmetic that the characters were forced to do every day.
The house at 124 Bluestone Road is haunted by the past it refuses to forget, and the ghost is the cost of that choice.
The community returns to help, and the women sing outside the house, turning the ledger back toward care.
The novel asks the reader to do the accounting the characters were forced to do, and to remember them.
